metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in New Albany, PA | Bradford County
metaDescription: New Albany, PA in Bradford County's dry-gas Marcellus core. We buy mineral and royalty rights directly, with honest evaluation of mature well production.
heroLead: New Albany sits in the hill country of northern Bradford County, and the ridges around it turned out to hold some of the earliest and most productive dry-gas Marcellus wells in the entire state.
intro: Bradford County drew intense operator interest starting in the mid-2000s, and New Albany and the surrounding townships were part of that first wave. Families here have generally held their leases longer than most royalty owners in Pennsylvania, which means a lot of local interests come with more than a decade of production history to evaluate.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around New Albany directly. Given how long some of these wells have been producing, we take real time reviewing the full history rather than a snapshot of recent months.

sections.heading: Hill Country, Deep History
paragraphs: The Marcellus rock under this part of Bradford County has proven consistently productive, and operators concentrated significant early drilling around New Albany and neighboring townships. That head start means the decline curves here are well established, which actually makes valuation more straightforward than a newer, less-tested well.
As dry-gas production, statements here don't carry the liquids-processing deductions found in wet-gas counties, though gathering and compression costs remain standard.

sections.heading: Long-Held Leases and Their Terms
paragraphs: Some of the earliest Bradford County leases were negotiated before the current landscape of royalty protections took shape, so it's worth reviewing your specific lease's deduction and renewal language carefully. We research this through the Bradford County Recorder of Deeds in Towanda alongside your division order.
If your lease has been amended or ratified over the years, which happens with long-held agreements, we account for that in our review.

sections.heading: Evaluating a Well Past Its Peak
paragraphs: A well into its production tail can still hold real value, especially with over a decade of documented history to work from. We'll walk through your statements with you before discussing an offer.

faqs.question: My family's lease near New Albany is one of the oldest in the area. Does that hurt its value?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Older, well-documented production often makes valuation more confident, though we do check whether the lease's specific terms are favorable.

faqs.question: Is a well that's been producing for over ten years still worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often yes. Long-producing Marcellus wells settle into a steady lower-volume tail that can continue for years, and that ongoing production carries value.

faqs.question: How do you account for lease amendments over the years?
faqs.answer: We research recorded amendments and ratifications through the county recorder as part of our title review, since they can affect royalty terms.
